title: Microsoft Entra ID: identity-verified account recovery for users who lose all sign-in methods (Android, iOS, desktop)
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports its recovery controls, licensing and disabled-by-default policy. It correctly distinguishes the overdue roadmap target from documented preview capabilities and preserves the Android Management API exception.

claims.claim: The feature is Microsoft Entra ID Account Recovery.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra: ID Account Recovery

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Account recovery restores access after a user loses all registered authentication methods.
claims.quote: enables users to regain access to their organizational accounts when they lose all registered authentication methods

claims.claim: Self-service password reset requires at least one surviving authentication method.
claims.quote: Unlike self-service password reset (SSPR), which requires users to retain at least one authentication method

claims.claim: Recovery re-establishes identity trust through third-party verification rather than manual help-desk verification.
claims.quote: account recovery re-establishes trust in a user's identity through third-party identity verification before restoring access.

claims.claim: Recovery uses Verified ID and Face Check.
claims.quote: Uses Microsoft Entra Verified ID and Face Check alongside third-party identity verification providers available through the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Scope; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Recovery is disabled by default for new and existing tenants and requires administrator enablement.
claims.quote: the policy is disabled by default for both new and existing tenants. Enable the policy before users can use account recovery.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Users need Microsoft Entra ID P1 to use account recovery.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license to use account recovery.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Face Check licence is required, through Entra Suite or standalone.
claims.quote: A Face Check license is also required, either through Entra Suite or standalone.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Recovery requires an identity verification provider subscription through Microsoft Security Store.
claims.quote: For All, Onboarding, or Recovery, select Identity Verification Provider. Configure and purchase the provider through the Microsoft Security Store. Select the provider after its status shows Subscribed.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The provider cost depends on the Microsoft Security Store offer subscribed to.
claims.quote: The identity verification provider cost depends on the offer you subscribe to in the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: Entitlement is mixed: Entra ID P1, Face Check through Suite or standalone, and separately purchased provider services.
claims.quote: Face Check is included as a full capability in the Microsoft Entra Suite. If your scenario uses an identity verification provider, purchase the provider's services separately through the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enable recovery at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) > Account recovery policy.
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview). In Account recovery settings, enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API for tenant Account recovery policy enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph account recovery policy enable settings API; accountRecoveryPolicy isEnabled. Opened recovery enablement and beta authenticationMethodsPolicy references; no recovery-policy enablement operation found.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator manages Account recovery settings.
claims.quote: The Authentication Policy Administrator role to manage Account recovery settings.

claims.claim: Creating a profile, including a Production profile, does not enable the tenant recovery policy.
claims.quote: For a recovery profile, Production mode alone doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: TAP issuance is on by default but does not itself enable tenant recovery.
claims.quote: Issue Temporary Access Pass on | Default for new and existing tenants. The default TAP issuance setting doesn't enable account recovery for your tenant.

claims.claim: The TAP setting is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) > Actions after recovery > Issue Temporary Access Pass.
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview). Use Actions after recovery in Account recovery settings ... Issue Temporary Access Pass

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API to configure recovery TAP issuance or automatic stale-credential cleanup.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph account recovery issueTemporaryAccessPass policy; staleCredentialCleanup settings API. Opened recovery settings and beta authenticationMethodsPolicy; results for ordinary TAP creation/configuration do not set recovery actions.

claims.claim: Turning TAP issuance off for TAP-free registration is an explicit preview option.
claims.quote: Issue Temporary Access Pass off | Explicit preview opt-in. Successful account validation grants access to registration in the same recovery session without a TAP on supported devices.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Stale-credential cleanup requires explicit preview opt-in with TAP issuance off.
claims.quote: Stale credential cleanup | Off by default; explicitly opt in during preview with TAP issuance off.

claims.claim: When passkey attestation is required, the TAP-free path is supported only on Android.
claims.quote: When passkey attestation is required, turning off TAP issuance is supported only on Android. iOS continues to receive a TAP

claims.claim: Android Management API users should keep TAP issuance on and receive a TAP at completion.
claims.quote: For users enrolled through Android Management API (AM API), keep TAP issuance on and configure recovery to issue a TAP at completion instead of requiring passkey setup.

claims.claim: Stale credential cleanup is in the same Actions after recovery section as TAP issuance.
claims.quote: Use Actions after recovery in Account recovery settings to choose how users register replacement methods. ... Stale credential cleanup

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The profile wizard follows Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles > Create profile > Profile purpose > Recovery > Profile mode > User group selection > Identity Verification Provider > Configure account validation.
claims.quote: Go to Verified ID > ID verification profiles. ... select Profiles > Create profile ... Select Profile purpose ... select Recovery ... profile mode ... User group selection ... select Identity Verification Provider ... On Configure account validation

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles creates a profile with issuer, validation and usage configuration.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/identity/verifiedId/profiles; verifiedIdProfileConfiguration ... accepted issuer, claims binding, and credential type; verifiedIdUsageConfigurations ... usage purpose

claims.claim: verifiedIdUsageConfigurations sets the usage purpose; recovery is supported.
claims.quote: purpose ... Sets the supported scenarios for a Verified ID profile. Currently only recovery is supported.

claims.claim: verifiedIdProfileConfiguration configures the issuer and claim validation.
claims.quote: "verifiedIdProfileConfiguration": { "type": "verifiedIdentity", "acceptedIssuer": "did:web:eu.did-dev.contoso.io", ... "claimValidation": { "isEnabled": true, "customExtensionId": "00aa00aa-bb11-cc22-dd33-44ee44ee44ee" } }

claims.claim: The profile API documents no user-group assignment.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph verifiedIdProfile verifiedIdUsageConfiguration group assignment include exclude. Read create-profile request properties, usage resource and profile-resource search excerpt; no group property or assignment relationship documented.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least-privileged role for profile creation through Graph.
claims.quote: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: The global exclusion is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview) > Global exclusions > Account onboarding and recovery (Preview).
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview). Under Global exclusions, enable the Account onboarding and recovery (Preview) exclusion.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: PATCH /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings configures the tenant-wide exclusion.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings ... "exclusions": { "allResourcesExclusions": { "userActionExclusions": [ { "state": "enabled", "userAction": "accountrecovery" } ] } }

claims.claim: The global onboarding and recovery exclusion is a preview setting.
claims.quote: Enable the global onboarding and recovery exclusion (preview)

claims.claim: The deciding request property is exclusions.allResourcesExclusions.userActionExclusions.
claims.quote: "exclusions": { "allResourcesExclusions": { "userActionExclusions": [ { "state": "enabled", "userAction": "accountrecovery" } ] } }

claims.claim: The userAction identifier for the exclusion is accountrecovery.
claims.quote: userAction | String | The user action identifier, for example, accountrecovery.

claims.claim: The exclusion supports state enabled or disabled.
claims.quote: enabled | The exclusion is enabled. disabled | The exclusion is disabled.

claims.claim: Updates must supply the complete desired userActionExclusions collection.
claims.quote: When updating userActionExclusions, supply the complete desired collection, not only the entries that changed.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta APIs are not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Recovery starts when the user identifies the account at sign-in and indicates they cannot access it.
claims.quote: The user provides their account identifier at sign-in and indicates they can't access their account.

claims.claim: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider in the applicable profile.
claims.quote: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider specified in their applicable profile.

claims.claim: After provider verification, the user receives a Verified ID credential stored in Microsoft Authenticator.
claims.quote: Upon successful verification, the user receives a verifiable credential (Verified ID) stored in Microsoft Authenticator.

claims.claim: The user presents the new Verified ID to Entra ID for validation.
claims.quote: The user presents their newly acquired Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID. The system validates the credential's authenticity.

claims.claim: Account validation can use the profile's directory claim mappings.
claims.quote: Account validation then uses the profile's configured directory claim mappings, a custom authentication extension, or both.

claims.claim: Account validation can use a custom authentication extension alone or alongside directory matching.
claims.quote: Custom authentication extensions can supplement directory matching or replace it entirely.

claims.claim: Successful recovery normally issues a TAP and guides the user to register replacement methods such as passkeys.
claims.quote: By default, the user receives a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) with limited validity and is guided through registering new authentication methods, such as passkeys.

claims.claim: Identity verification processes government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.
claims.quote: Identity verification involves processing government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Providers have their own privacy and retention policies in their Security Store offers.
claims.quote: Identity verification providers have their own privacy and data retention policies as part of the verification offer from the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: A custom authentication extension is optional.
claims.quote: Custom authentication extensions — Optional Azure Function, Logic App, or REST API endpoints that add organization-specific account validation logic during recovery.

claims.claim: Extension-processed data stays within the organisation's trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data processed by the custom authentication extension stays within the organization's trust boundary.

claims.claim: Only the extension match result is returned to the recovery flow.
claims.quote: No organizational data is shared with Microsoft — only the match result is returned to the account recovery flow.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that name-only matching may not provide enough assurance for high-risk accounts.
claims.quote: Name-only matching may not provide sufficient assurance for high-risk accounts.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests custom extensions to validate additional claims for sensitive populations.
claims.quote: For sensitive user populations, consider enabling a custom authentication extension to validate additional claims beyond first and last name.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Conditional Access can protect account recovery.
claims.quote: Do Conditional Access policies apply during account recovery? Yes. Conditional Access can add an extra layer of security during account recovery.

claims.claim: Terms of use, Require authentication strength and most other Entra-specific controls are unsupported for onboarding and recovery.
claims.quote: The following controls aren't supported for these journeys: Terms of use. Require authentication strength. Most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls also aren't supported for this action.

claims.claim: Unsupported recovery policy requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.
claims.quote: Unsupported recovery policy requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.

claims.claim: Enabled cleanup with TAP issuance off deletes all old registered methods after recovery and replacement-passkey registration succeed.
claims.quote: Cleanup is available only when TAP issuance is off. ... When cleanup is enabled, it deletes all previously registered authentication methods after both recovery and registration of the replacement passkey succeed. The newly registered passkey isn't deleted.
